From: monica_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: FinCo DPA redlines (round 1) — internal counsel comments

Aditya / team — I reviewed FinCo's annotated DPA (attached) and included counsel notes below on the key asks. High level: we can't accept a blanket "EU-only storage" obligation; operationally we rely on region tagging and customer configuration, and some processing (e.g., model updates, analytics) may require US-hosted services. Proposed approach:

1) Data localization / storage clause
- Customer request: store/process EU personal data in EU only.
- Counsel recommendation: propose compromise language that requires primary storage within the EU and a commitment that processing in other regions will be used only when necessary for service delivery, subject to SCCs and documented safeguards. Provide an explicit list of categories that must remain in-region (e.g., production user data) while logs/telemetry may be aggregated outside the EU in pseudonymized form.
- Suggested text (for redline): "Redwood shall make commercially reasonable efforts to store and process Customer personal data primarily within the European Economic Area (EEA). Where processing outside the EEA is necessary for service delivery, Redwood shall ensure an adequate transfer mechanism (e.g., SCCs) and implement technical and organizational safeguards as described in Annex A. Customer may request confirmation of the location of primary storage for its account."

2) EU→US transfers
- We'll supply executed SCC templates and a short Transfer Impact Assessment summary. We should avoid committing to a legal opinion.

3) Subprocessors
- We can provide current subprocessor inventory and 30-day notice for additions. For objection rights, we normally allow objections for subprocessors that will process personal data in a way that would create a material risk; we can offer an expedited review path for critical customers.

4) Execution / e-sign
- DocuSign is preferred (audit trail, envelope templates). AdobeSign is possible but requires extra validation from Ops. Recommend we plan for DocuSign and include alternate AdobeSign instructions in the execution checklist in case FinCo insists.

Attachments: privacy_note_counsel_comments.pdf (pdf, 85KB) — contains inline clause suggestions and Annex A TO&Cs summary.

I'll prepare a counterproposal redline with the suggested language and send by 2026-06-01. Rafael, FYI in case we need pricing concessions tied to localization requirements.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Privacy Counsel (Legal LLP) <privacy@legalllp.com>

Subject: Re: FinCo DPA redlines (round 1) — follow up on subprocessors and SCCs

Monica / Aditya — thanks for the prompt reply and suggested compromise language. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Subprocessor inventory: we need the current list (names, country of operation, brief description of processing) and a commitment to update the list within 30 days of changes. The customer will reserve the right to object to a new subprocessor that will process EU personal data.
- SCCs: please confirm you will provide executed SCCs (EU Commission module) or adopt Redwood's SCC annex. If transfers involve US-based analytics vendors, counsel will likely ask for specific supplemental safeguards and a short TIA.
- Evidence: are you able to provide SOC 2 Type II and a summary of encryption/key management practices? That will speed internal approvals.

We can accept the "primary storage in EEA" approach but need precise language about what "primary" means (e.g., physical location of production storage for the customer's account). Also want to avoid open-ended "commercially reasonable efforts" unless accompanied by measurable controls.

Please send the subprocessor CSV and SCC template by the end of week if possible.

Regards,
Privacy Counsel
Legal LLP
